duplicate_review.method: deterministic atom keys and manual scope review

consistency_findings: The main article describes S9–S14 as sensitivity analyses using more conservative 99% confidence intervals, while captions for some individual sensitivity figures still label estimates as 95% CIs. This source-level inconsistency was preserved rather than silently corrected.
The article reports no statistically significant increase in UTI versus placebo; genital-tract-infection estimates are sparse and imprecise for several therapies.
limitations: This is a secondary-source LiteratureAtom extraction; the cited randomized trials should be extracted separately when primary-study atoms are required.
All main Table 2 and Table 3 network estimates versus placebo were atomized. The complete active-vs-active S3–S14 matrix cells were reconciled in coverage/SEA but not atomized individually.
